name: Feed watch for school, PTA, town and library sites (RSS/Atom)
description: A watcher with no model in it that checks a short list of feeds a few times a day and passes on only new post titles, for the sources that never email: the school blog, the PTA site, town notices, library events, the sports league.
example: Trigger: the 16:00 job finds one new item on the PTA feed and adds 'PTA: book fair volunteers needed (new today)' to the school digest.
how: Build the blogwatcher CLI in the admin account from a pinned, reviewed commit and install the binary for the happy user; the bundled skill documents add, blogs, scan, articles and read-all. Tony registers the feeds by hand. A cron command payload (--command-argv, no model call, created by the operator) runs a wrapper script that scans, parses the tool's plain text output, prints unread titles with their source name (length-capped, links dropped unless the host matches the registered feed), marks them read, and prints NO_REPLY when nothing is new. Delivery is announce to the parents under the G001 notification policy, or the titles are handed to the F056 school digest as quoted data.
depends_on: A Go toolchain or prebuilt blogwatcher binary for the happy user
Each site actually publishing a feed
A blogwatcher binary built in the admin account from a pinned, reviewed commit and installed for the happy user
First check which of the family's school, PTA, town, library and league sites publish a feed; if fewer than three do, drop this
caveats: Many school portals and social pages publish no feed; blogwatcher's HTML fallback needs a CSS selector per site and breaks on redesigns.
A feed reader app or search alerts already do this for a parent who will open them; the gain is one combined digest.
blogwatcher keeps its state in its own SQLite file in the happy user's home, one more item for the G007 backup list.
Titles only; reading a post's body is a research-agent task (F019).

Command payloads run on the Gateway host as the happy user, outside the Colima sandbox and outside agent tool policy, so the blogwatcher binary and the wrapper are trusted code next to every family secret. The project is a small personal repository with no tagged releases: build a reviewed, pinned commit rather than installing @latest, and give the job a minimal environment.
blogwatcher documents only coloured terminal output, with no JSON mode, so the wrapper has to parse text and needs a fixture test.
safety:
It runs as an operator-authored command payload inside the scheduler with no model and no agent tools, so untrusted feed text cannot steer anything; it is only relayed, shortened and stripped of foreign links. The price is that the command runs on the host as the happy user with no sandbox, so the binary is pinned and reviewed and the wrapper gets a minimal environment. If titles are ever given to a model for the digest, that model must be the tool-less school-mail reader, never

-main. Requests go only to the feed addresses Tony registered. The bundled skill itself is not loaded into any agent.
unverified: Whether blogwatcher offers machine-readable output or the wrapper must parse its text output
Which of this family's school and town sites expose feeds
How stable blogwatcher's text output is across versions (its README documents no machine-readable mode)

name: Recipe link to ingredients and steps
description: Text a recipe link and get the ingredient list and the steps without the life story and the ads, scaled to the number of people, with an offer to add what is missing to the grocery list.
example: "<recipe link> What do I need for this for six people?"
how:
Mechanism choice: plain `web_fetch`, which reduces a page to its main content; schema.org also defines a Recipe vocabulary (`recipeIngredient`, `recipeInstructions`, `recipeYield`) that recipe sites can embed.

-main hands the URL to research with `sessions_spawn` and `completionTarget: "parent"`; research fetches, makes one `llm-task` call with a small schema (title, yield, ingredients[], steps[], source URL, fetched-at) and returns that JSON as its result;

-main scales quantities and proposes list items (F032), written only after a yes. The schema shapes the answer but is not an enforced gate: the result reaches

-main as ordinary sub-agent text. Fallbacks in order: WEB-02 `text` action for script-rendered pages; a host-side `summarize --extract` wrapper for video recipes (the CLI is not installed; pin `--firecrawl off` in the wrapper).
caveats: The fetch returns the readable article text. It is not documented to return the page's embedded Recipe data, so the model parses ingredients from prose and can drop a line. Always include the source link.
Some recipe sites sit behind bot walls or paywalls and return nothing; say so instead of guessing.
The phone's reader view and recipe-keeper apps already do the clean-up; the added value is the hand-off to the shared grocery list.
Scaling quantities is arithmetic done by a language model: fine for a stew, worth a second look for baking.
'Add what is missing' assumes Happy knows what is in the kitchen. It does not; in practice it offers the whole ingredient list and the parent strikes what they have.

The summarize CLI named as the video fallback takes any address and has its own third-party extraction fallbacks. A wrapper must pass `--firecrawl off`, hold no third-party keys, and check the address itself (https, public host), because OpenClaw's SSRF policy does not cover a host-side CLI.
The reading half works the day the research agent exists; the grocery hand-off, which is the part the phone does not already do, waits on the Reminders bridge.
On today's config no agent has `web_fetch` or `sessions_spawn` and the `llm-task` plugin is not enabled; all three are config changes that arrive with F019 and F082.
safety:
The untrusted page is read by research only, and nothing private goes to research: an address and a serving count. What comes back to

-main is text written by a model that has just read an untrusted page. Running it through `llm-task` with a schema fixes its shape, not its content: a step string can still carry instructions, and nothing in the platform forces the check to run. The limits that hold are that

-main has no browser or fetch and its recipients are pinned to the family. List writes wait for the parent's yes, a prompt rule that is acceptable at grocery-list stakes.
unverified: Whether web_fetch output ever includes a page's JSON-LD blocks: a search of the installed code found no JSON-LD handling in the fetch extractor, but no live recipe page was fetched.
How many of the recipe sites this family uses embed schema.org Recipe data.

Whether a plugin hook can enforce a schema on a sub-agent's result before

-main reads it.
Whether llm-task's isolated completion works through the family's per-person custom provider ids; its allowed-model list has to name them.

review_notes: A good low-risk workflow with a safe holder. Two claims need fixing: the schema check is something the model chooses to run, not a platform gate on what research hands back; and the version worth having is 'build', because the grocery hand-off needs the Reminders bridge and neither research nor web_fetch exists yet.

Mechanism and sources are sound and it is config-only once the research agent exists. The safety claim is too strong: llm-task validates one completion inside research, but what research hands back to

-main is ordinary sub-agent text that nothing schema-checks, and a string field can hold any text anyway. Also, the `summarize` fallback is not installed and has its own Firecrawl switch.

name: Severe-weather, snow-day and weather-chore watch
description: Both parents get a three-line heads-up once per new winter storm, wind, flood or freeze alert for home, with a school-night closure reminder and a chore checklist.
how: Host command job, `--command-argv '["node","scripts/nws-alerts.mjs"]'` every 30 minutes, polls api.weather.gov `/alerts/active?point=`, dedups on alert `id`, prints `NO_REPLY` otherwise; zero model calls.
unverified: That an NWS update to an existing alert arrives under a new id pointing back through `references`: the fields were seen, their semantics were not read, so the dedup rule needs a test.
The current weather plugin returns alerts without an id (read in ~/src/happy-config, not a citable source kind), which is why the script calls the API directly.
The Apple Weather app's own severe-weather notification switch: Apple's page loaded only its table of contents in this run.

name: Product recall watch matched to what the family owns (CPSC)
description: Happy checks the Consumer Product Safety Commission's recall list each day and texts only when a recall matches something the family owns or a kid-product keyword, instead of the parents skimming every recall email. A query for recalls since 20 Sep 2026 returned 31 in under three weeks, so the filter is the feature.
example: Trigger: a new recall whose product name contains a brand on the family's owned-items list. Text: 'CPSC recall 26-xxx: <product title>. Hazard: burn. Remedy: refund. Link: cpsc.gov/...'
how: Operator-created command job (no model): `--cron '15 7 * * *' --command-argv '["node","scripts/cpsc-recalls.mjs"]' --announce --to <parent>`. The script requests `https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices/Recall?format=json&RecallDateStart=<last run>` (date filter only, nothing about the family in the URL), keeps seen RecallID values in a state file, and matches Title, Products, Manufacturers, Retailers and ProductUPCs locally against (a) owned-item keywords exported from family.json5 or the F034 registry and (b) a short kid-category list. Owned match: one text now. Category match: held for a Sunday digest of at most five. Otherwise `NO_REPLY`.
depends_on: F034 home systems registry or a hand-kept owned-items list
caveats: The match is only as good as the owned-items list; substring matching on brand names will produce some false positives and miss unlisted items.
CPSC already offers its own recall emails, an RSS feed and an app. Happy adds the match against the family's own list, not earlier notice.
No key or rate limit is documented on the API page; poll once a day, not more.
Vehicles and car seats are handled by NHTSA, food and medicine by FDA and USDA; see SRC-04 and SRC-05.
Run one job per parent with its own seen-id state file; with a shared file the second parent's job finds nothing new and stays silent.
safety: No model runs in the job. Recall titles are published by CPSC but name companies and products, so the script prints them through a fixed template, stripped to plain letters, digits and spaces, capped in length, with only the cpsc.gov link. The request reveals nothing about the household. Delivery is the job's pinned parent target. The installed source mirrors a delivered announce line into the session transcript of the agent that owns the job, so that agent can read the line on a later turn: own these jobs with a memory-less, tool-less agent, or accept the sanitised line in the parent agent's transcript.
unverified: Formal terms of use or rate limit for the recall web service (the page read gives none).
Whether text announced by a command job is also written into the receiving agent's session transcript; the script keeps output short and templated in case it is.
Documentation for the RecallDateStart parameter (it is not on the API information page read; it is confirmed only by the live response).
Which agent's session receives the mirrored line for a command job, to be checked by reading the transcript after the first run.
